Performance, under the hood · check

Know Where the time goes already?

One question for each of the 5 puzzles in this module. A right answer marks that puzzle as passed, so you can jump ahead. A wrong one tells you which puzzle to start with. Nothing is sent anywhere: it's saved in this browser.

Puzzle 0: Threads take turns

A phone has eight cores and twenty threads are ready to run. What happens to the other twelve?

Not quite. Leaving the queue is for threads waiting for something; ready threads queue. Learn it in puzzle 0 →

Not quite. A core runs one thread at a time; the rest wait. Learn it in puzzle 0 →

Right. Ready but no core means waiting in the queue.

Puzzle 1: What a trace is

CPU usage was 60% during startup. What does a trace add?

Right. A number says how much; a trace says what and when.

Not quite. It adds them up; the trace keeps them apart, in time. Learn it in puzzle 1 →

Not quite. A trace isn't a better number; it's the timeline behind it. Learn it in puzzle 1 →

Puzzle 2: A photo or a diary

A function runs for 50 µs, once, between two snapshots. Which tool can miss it entirely?

Not quite. A trace section records whatever span you wrap; the risk of missing it is sampling's. Learn it in puzzle 2 →

Not quite. Instrumentation records every method's start and end, however short. Learn it in puzzle 2 →

Right. A snapshot misses what started and ended between two snapshots.

Puzzle 3: Reading the flames

In a flame chart, format() is drawn left of parseJson(). What does that tell you?

Right. Width is time; position isn't.

Not quite. A caller and its callees are stacked, not side by side. Learn it in puzzle 3 →

Not quite. That's a call chart. In a flame chart the order is by width, not by when. Learn it in puzzle 3 →

Puzzle 4: Slow isn't always busy

In another trace, a 120 ms main-thread span is 110 ms Sleeping. What will making its code faster save?

Not quite. Only Running time is code running; Sleeping is waiting for something else. Learn it in puzzle 4 →

Right. Faster code shortens only Running.

Not quite. Sleeping ends when what it waits for arrives, not when the CPU is faster. Learn it in puzzle 4 →
